_doc: The decks of cloud a battle's nebula plumes rise between (src/Game/View/NebulaDeck.cs, read into src/Game/View/nebula_deck.gdshader; owner, 2026-11-10: "The clouds need to stretch up in columns of varying widths across the map", "make a cloud mesh for top and bottom of nebula and fade out the edges, so it looks like the nebula columns are connected to a larger structure above and below the map"). A battle with any plume has two decks, one above the battle plane and one below, mirror images; every plume's column reaches from one into the other (NebulaPlume.Cover). underside_km is how far the deck's face toward the battle stands off the plane and thickness_km how deep the deck is past it; hang_km how far that face hangs and lifts across the deck (its billows, by the noise); join_km how much further the face reaches toward the plane round the root of a column that reaches it, and funnel_km how far out from the column's edge that funnel spreads, so each column runs up into a funnel of the deck; margin_km how far past the outermost column the deck is whole, and fade_km how far beyond that it thins away to nothing (its edge); planet_clear_x how far round a planet the deck is clear, in the planet's radii, so a planet is never buried in it; coverage how much of the deck is cloud (0 to 1); absorption_per_km how fast its cloud swallows light; contrast how far its density varies inside, as a plume's (data/space/plumes.json); base_km the size of its billows (one repeat of the noise) and detail_km of the wisps that eat their edges, erosion how deep those bite (0 to 1); drift_per_s how fast the billows move, in repeats a second; glow_strength how much its thin edges glow (0 to 2). The face toward the battle lies in the deck's own shadow where the sun is beyond it, and takes a fill of the light the battle's clouds throw back (fill, 0 to 1 of its lit colour); each column darkens the same way as it climbs into that deck, so the two meet in one shade. column_shade is the share of the sun a column's own cloud lets through to its face (0 to 1): a deck's face sees the sun across open space, a column shades itself through its own depth, so the deck takes the column's share and the two read as one cloud of one colour. variety is how much its colour and shade vary across it in broad patches (0 to 1; owner, 2026-11-10: "give the decks some varying colors so its not all uniform (and vertex color shading)"); far off it fades into the sky behind it, from far_from_km to far_to_km from the camera ("fade the decks out so they blend in with the background too"). Only a column that reaches a deck has a funnel in it (NebulaDef.Forms). Its colours are the plumes' own looks (data/space/plumes.json), each column's round its root and their mean between. A battle among plumes is also hazed (owner, 2026-11-10: "add in a general layer of fog too, so detail in the distance fades into fog"): fog_km is the distance at which a thing shows through a little over a third of the haze, fog_lit where its colour sits between the plumes' shadow and their light (0 to 1, each look by the area it covers), fog_sky how much of it lies over the sky (0 to 1); the clouds take the same haze at their own depth. style is how the nebula is drawn (owner, 2026-11-10: "lets see how all one or the other looks", "third technique to try out: crab-breezes cloud system", "cheap 3d billboards with lighting"): volume (every column and deck marched cloud), meshes (puffs of displaced mesh) or billboards (Crab Breeze's lit camera-facing puffs); the two puff styles fill each column inside its own shape and lay each deck as a field of puffs deck_puff_km apart; a run or a still may name another with --nebula-style=. The view only. Provisional until the owner has seen them (survey NP9).
